text:
Riley Park: Noticed an odd billing leak in canary: clients that reconnect during websocket half-close end up with stale in-flight credits. Console shows a slow ramp in 'active_token_seconds' for the tenant even after client disconnected.
Nina Rao: Repro?
Riley Park: Steps: open WS, send long-running stream, trigger proxy FIN (simulate netem delay), client reconnects to different edge -> server creates a new session and old session never garbage-collected due to missing close event.
Omar Khalid: Hmm. We rely on finalizers on socket close to decrement in-flight tokens and release quota. If proxy doesn't surface EOF, finalizer doesn't run. Do we have tombstones?
Ethan Brooks: We create tombstones via session-lease with default TTL 30s, but the shard-level GC sometimes misses if lease refreshs intermittently. Also recall we increment quota at accept time (optimistic).
Jules Marin: UX problem: ops sees rising cost in console and paged on quota alerts. We should avoid noisy alerts while we fix. Two prongs: immediate UI smoothing + backend fix.
Nina Rao: Backend options: 1) lower tombstone TTL to 5s (risk: false evictions on flaky networks) 2) add a lightweight session-heartbeat from client to claim ownership on reconnect path 3) flip quota increment to post-confirm (adds 1 RTT). Thoughts?
Omar Khalid: We can do hybrid: keep optimistic increment but emit a compensating 'reconcile' event if GC finds duplicate resume/session within tombstone window. That avoids blocking accept path.
Ethan Brooks: Agree. Implementation: on accept, write session record with claim_nonce and increment optimistic counter. Spawn background reconciler task that does atomic compare-and-swap in central store; if CAS fails, emit "quota_compensation" event which billing pipeline can consume to decrement.
Riley Park: Important: add metric 'ws_stale_inflight_detected' and tag with tenant_id and edge. Also emit tracing span for the reconcile path.
Jules Marin: UI: add a transient annotation on tenant cost time-series: "possible stale-inflight detected, reconciling" with a link to the reconcile metric. Also mute quota alerting for reconciled windows (configurable flag).
Nina Rao: What about routing policy? If reconnect lands on different region, we might accept honorably. Maybe we need 'sticky reconnect' for last_event_id within 10s to prefer prior shard. That reduces cross-shard races.
Omar Khalid: Sticky preference is fine as an optimization. We'll implement 'soft affinity' on accept: prefer shard that last reported resume_id if within 10s, else normal selection. No strong consistency changes.
Ethan Brooks: I'll add claim_nonce to logs: format `cn=<hex>` and include span id. Also dump last_event_id in accept logs.
deploy-bot: Rolling: reconciler background task -> canary eu-central in 20m.
ops-bot: Created INF-9033: "ws: reconcile stale in-flight credits + console smoothing" assigned to Jules. ETA 4d.
Riley Park: Action items: 1) reconciler PR (Ethan) 2) soft affinity routing (Omar) 3) metrics+logs (Ethan+Riley) 4) console smoothing flag + alert mute (Jules) 5) watch canary for ws_stale_inflight_detected (Nina).
Jules Marin: Quick UX note: make smoothing non-destructive by default (only hides alert, doesn't change raw billing data).
Nina Rao: Also consider adding an operator endpoint to force-GC a resume_id for emergency corrections.
Omar Khalid: Good idea; admin API `POST /admin/resume/{resume_id}/evict?force=true` with idempotent semantics. I'll spec this in PR.
Riley Park: Cool. I'll post a follow-up once canary metrics settle. Thanks all :rocket:
